brand.name: KnotTrace
brand.trayNote: Closing the window keeps the app running in the tray.
brand.trayNoteShort: Runs in the tray when closed.
brand.disclaimer: KnotTrace is a network companion — indicators and assists, not antivirus.

protect.processReviewHint: Applies reversible DNS/Connect when available; marks the rest reviewed. Indicators are not auto-fixed.

pathJournal.title: Path / exit journal
pathJournal.empty: Run a few health checks to see recent path, egress IP, shape, and grade.

overviewTip.pathTruth: KnotTrace’s job is path truth — where the break is — not a speed boost.

reason.tunnel: A tunnel or proxy path is active — begin with Tunnel compare for overhead vs Direct.
reason.upstream: Upstream pool claim looks impaired — review pool proof before thrashing nodes.
reason.proxy: Proxy-only site failures show up — compare proxy vs Direct on Proxy path.
reason.pathBreak: Path break shows a hop other than none — start with that classification.
reason.egress: Public egress looks unstable or changed — open Egress timeline first.
reason.default: Start with Path break for the active path and hop classification.

connectPage.unsupportedSummary: Connect Assist needs Mihomo or sing-box with external-controller (or a saved API URL in Advanced). KnotTrace still diagnoses path and proxy without switching nodes.
connectPage.measuredProxy: Proxy path comparisons and upstream pool proof
connectPage.measuredTunnel: Tunnel compare (VPN / Tor / proxy vs Direct)
connectPage.openNetwork: Open Network or Overview for that evidence — this page does not invent an Apply action without an API.
connectPage.noGroupsSummary: The proxy API responded but no switchable groups were listed. Check the controller config, then re-open Connect.

nextSteps.title: What to do next
nextSteps.pendingDescription: Run a health check to get a symptom-specific next-step plan.
nextSteps.recurrence: Recurring pattern: {shape} appeared in {count} of your last {window} checks.

hero.checkFailed: Last check failed — use Retry in the banner above.
hero.noReport: Run a health check to see how this connection is doing.
hero.goodDefault: No obvious problems on this check. You can keep using the network as usual.
hero.lookCloser: This check found something worth a closer look below.
hero.captiveConfirmed: This Wi‑Fi needs sign-in before the internet works. Finish the portal in a browser, then re-check.
hero.captiveSuspected: Sign-in may be required on this network. Finish any portal (or switch networks), then re-check.
hero.bufferbloat: Latency jumps under load (bufferbloat) — not a raw speed problem. Check router SQM/QoS if calls lag during downloads.
hero.tunnelExpected: A VPN, Tor, or proxy path is active. Slower is expected — local repair will not speed up this tunnel.
hero.tunnelBufferbloat: Tunnel overhead and under-load lag (bufferbloat) are both in play — not only one. Check Network for tunnel compare and stability.
hero.torSocksDown: Tor SOCKS is not reachable. Fix or wait for the Tor client bootstrap — this is not evidence your ISP link is down.
hero.partialLocal: Some sites fail, but the break looks local first — fix the local hop before blaming a destination or node.
hero.partialDns: Some sites fail with a DNS-shaped break. Check resolvers before thrashing proxy nodes.
hero.partialActivePath: Some sites fail on the active path. Compare Upstream pool / tunnel evidence before a careful Connect change.
hero.partialDestination: Some sites fail while the local path looks OK — likely destination, filter, or policy, not a local repair job.
hero.pathAttention: Latency looks fine, but the active path still shows a break — open Network for hop evidence.
hero.integrityAttention: Latency looks fine, but Protect has exposure or routing signals to review — not a malware verdict.
hero.pathAndIntegrity: Latency looks fine, but path and Protect both need a look — start with the evidence cards below.

path.expectationLocalFirst: Fix the local/path break first. Tunnel overhead is secondary until the local hop is healthy.
path.expectationTorSocksDown: Tor SOCKS is down — treat this as a Tor client/bootstrap issue, not a broken NIC.
path.expectationFallbackTor: Tor is for anonymity, not speed. Higher latency than Direct is expected — KnotTrace will not try to accelerate Tor.
path.expectationFallbackVpn: A VPN path is active. Extra latency is normal; local assists will not make the vendor tunnel faster.
path.expectationFallbackProxy: System proxy is active. Compare proxy vs Direct on Network — provider-side limits are not fixed by local repair.

copy.softSummary: Hints are weak on this check. Inspect Network details before changing DNS, proxy, or Protect settings.
copy.bufferbloatSummary: Bandwidth is probably fine; latency jumps when something uploads or downloads. Check router SQM/QoS — this is not a raw “slow ISP” problem.
copy.captiveConfirmedSummary: Open a browser, finish the hotspot portal, then re-check. Do not change DNS or proxy until the portal is done.
copy.captiveSuspectedSummary: This network may require a login page. Finish sign-in (or switch networks), then re-check before assists.
copy.pageStartTitle: Start with DNS and sign-in checks
copy.pageStartSummary: This looks more like a page-start delay than a raw bandwidth issue. Check DNS integrity first, then confirm the path is not behind a hotspot sign-in or proxy delay.
copy.partialThrashTitle: Stop thrashing nodes — upstream pool looks poor
copy.partialThrashSummary: Proxy-only failures recur across checks or exit IPs. Review Upstream pool proof; changing nodes rapidly will not fix a weak pool.
copy.partialTitle: Active path is impaired for some sites
copy.partialSummary: Some sites appear to fail only on this route. Check Upstream pool proof first, then consider at most one careful Connect Assist change if the claim is active-path only.
copy.partialLocalSummary: Site failures are present, but the break looks local (gateway, NIC, or client). Repair the local hop before blaming a destination or switching nodes.
copy.partialDnsTitle: DNS looks involved in these site failures
copy.partialDnsSummary: Reachability failures look DNS-shaped. Review DNS integrity / Assist before thrashing proxy nodes or assuming geo block.
copy.partialDestinationTitle: Site or policy may be blocking
copy.partialDestinationSummary: The local path looks OK while some destinations fail. This can be destination outage, filter, or geo/policy — open Network for path evidence; local repair will not unblock it.
copy.restrictedSummary: Guest or public network — finish any portal, avoid sensitive traffic until trusted, then re-check.
copy.tunnelThrashTitle: Tunnel path is limited by upstream quality
copy.tunnelThrashSummary: History shows recurring proxy-path impairment. Do not rotate exits to hunt speed — review the pool claim and change provider or traffic policy instead.
copy.tunnelSummary: A VPN, proxy, or Tor path may be adding latency or causing path-specific failures. Compare recommendations before switching anything manually.
copy.tunnelHonestyTitle: Slower is expected on this path
copy.tunnelHonestySummary: VPN, Tor, or proxy overhead is normal here. Local DNS or NIC repair will not speed up this tunnel — open Network for tunnel compare evidence.
copy.tunnelLocalFirstTitle: Fix local path before blaming the tunnel
copy.tunnelLocalFirstSummary: A tunnel is present, but the break looks local. Repair the local hop first; do not expect a node switch to fix a broken local path.
copy.tunnelBufferbloatTitle: Tunnel overhead and under-load lag both show up
copy.tunnelBufferbloatSummary: A VPN/Tor/proxy path adds expected overhead, and latency also jumps under load (bufferbloat). Open Network for tunnel compare and stability — local “speed” repair will not fix either alone.
copy.torSocksDownSummary: Tor SOCKS is not reachable. Wait for bootstrap or fix the Tor client — this is not an ISP outage signal.
copy.linkLocalSummary: The bottleneck looks close to your device or router. Review gateway latency, Wi-Fi vs Ethernet, and physical link quality before blaming the wider internet.
